The first lens implant came from a fighter plane. In the Battle of Britain in 1940, eye surgeon Harold Ridley found that splinters of clear plastic from aircraft canopies sat in pilots' eyes without harm.

Cataract surgery then removed the clouded lens and left patients in thick glasses. In 1947 a student asked why a lens could not be put back. At 43, Ridley had one cut from the same plastic by the optician John Pike, and on 29 November 1949 he operated at St Thomas' Hospital in London. The first lens was too thick, so the next was recalculated. His peers called it reckless, and he did not patent it.

Today 6 to 10 million cataract operations a year, and the lens implant is the standard treatment.
